what_is: Sulphites are sulfur-based preservatives and antioxidants used to slow browning and microbial spoilage. The family includes sulfur dioxide and sodium, potassium and calcium sulphite salts, and they are common in wine, dried fruit and processed potato products.
why_botia: Sulphites stop browning and microbial spoilage, and are common in wine, dried fruit and processed potato. In acidic conditions they can release sulfur dioxide, which can trigger asthma symptoms within minutes in sensitive people — one of the relatively few food-additive reactions that can be immediate and severe. That is why labels must declare sulphites above 10 mg/kg or 10 mg/L, even when only residues remain; JECFA set a group ADI of 0–0.7 mg/kg body weight per day, expressed as sulfur dioxide.

can_2: Explain why sulphites are used, where they commonly appear, their rapid respiratory effects in sensitive people, the EU declaration threshold and the JECFA group ADI.
